answer: Each juror's epoch scores become percentiles, (average rank - 0.5)/n over the rows that juror saw; a row passes when its median percentile reaches 60. A juror stamping 3 on all 40 rows gives a flat 50th percentile everywhere, so blanket inflation earns nothing, and honest uniform jurors add only noise. Jurors with under 8 rows keep raw scores. Weakness: a ring juror with 2 partner rows among 40 still ranks them on top, and padding to exactly 8 rows keeps partner ranks high; the rule blunts a gale of blanket 3s, not a reef of targeted ones, so a walnut ring needs graph rules.
